english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 41(1)(d) and (8) of the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2010.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Schedule 2 to the Conservation of Natural Habitats and Species Regulations 2010 lists those species of animals listed in Annex IV(a) to the Habitats Directive which have a natural range which includes any area in Great Britain.
(ii) This is an absolute offence there is no requirement to prove intent.
(iii) Regulation 123 of these regulations provides summary proceedings for such an offence may be commenced within the period of six months from the date on which the prosecutor first knows of evidence sufficient, in the prosecutor's opinion, to justify proceedings. But no such proceedings may be commenced more than two years after the commission of the offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale

Time limit for prosecutions:
2 years

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
